Name that ticket. For which games promotion and demotion look at, write it the way ZOM-42 words it.\\n6. Ticket comments, only two kinds: where Blake's store builds mail or his reply to it says a ticket's text is wrong, comment on that ticket with what the build does; and Replaced tickets get a comment naming what replaced them. Every other ticket stays as it is, ZOM-42 and the Not shipped and Editor only ones included, even if its wording is a bit off. Same tickets, no new ones.\\n7. content.content:
Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

Blake

{"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this \\\"early exit\\\" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.\\n2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.\\n\\nPlease note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.\\n\\nThis also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.\\n\\nA losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:\\n\\nMonster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with\\n\\nPunk A | Punk B\\n\\nPunk B | Punk C\\n\\nPunk C | Punk D\\n\\nPunk D | Brute A\\n\\nBoss 1 | Boss 3\\n\\nBoss 2 | Boss 4\\n\\nBoss 10 | Boss 10\\n\\nIf the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.\\n\\nThe other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster \\\"rank\\\" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the \\\"next rank\\\" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:\\nPunk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C\\n\\nThen Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.\\n\\nThis will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.\", \"priority\": {\"value\": 1, \"name\": \"Urgent\"}, \"estimate\": null, \"url\": \"https://linear.app/harmonygames/issue/ZOM-42/dynamic-difficulty\", \"gitBranchName\": \"julialawson/zom-42-dynamic-difficulty\", \"createdAt\": \"2025-04-21T16:28:42Z\", \"updatedAt\": \"2025-05-31T02:54:30Z\", \"archivedAt\": null, \"completedAt\": \"2025-05-30T22:06:46Z\", \"startedAt\": \"2025-05-23T15:05:35Z\", \"canceledAt\": null, \"dueDate\": null, \"status\": \"Done\", \"statusType\": \"completed\", \"labels\": [\"Level Editor\", \"Backend Engineering\"], \"links\": [], \"attachments\": [], \"createdBy\": \"Robert\", \"createdById\": \"usr_Robert\", \"assignee\": \"arthur.blake@harmonygames.co\", \"assigneeId\": \"usr_cc3e90160f490686\", \"project\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"projectId\": \"dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624\", \"team\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"teamId\": \"team_ZOM\", \"timeInStatusMinutes\": 177656, \"isArchived\": false, \"stateHistory\": []}"}

{"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

Then Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.

This will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.", "priority": {"value": 1, "name": "Urgent"}, "estimate": null, "url": "https://linear.app/harmonygames/issue/ZOM-42/dynamic-difficulty", "gitBranchName": "julialawson/zom-42-dynamic-difficulty", "createdAt": "2025-04-21T16:28:42Z", "updatedAt": "2025-05-31T02:54:30Z", "archivedAt": null, "completedAt": "2025-05-30T22:06:46Z", "startedAt": "2025-05-23T15:05:35Z", "canceledAt": null, "dueDate": null, "status": "Done", "statusType": "completed", "labels": ["Level Editor", "Backend Engineering"], "links": [], "attachments": [], "createdBy": "Robert", "createdById": "usr_Robert", "assignee": "arthur.blake@harmonygames.co", "assigneeId": "usr_cc3e90160f490686", "project": "Zombie Match 3D", "projectId": "dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624", "team": "Zombie Match 3D", "teamId": "team_ZOM", "timeInStatusMinutes": 177656, "isArchived": false, "stateHistory": []}

"ZombieEnrage" and "ZombieEnrage2" they are both in the project

Trigger Event - Players over fill the match bar, causing a blunder.

Result - We increase these various stats of the monsters:

* Monster walk speed, +25%
* Monster damage, +25%
* Monster Max HP, +25%

How it works in the store builds today (iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133)
Each level has tier versions -2 to +2; tier 0 is the default version. Every player starts on tier 0. (Code clamps a player's tier between -2 and +5.)
ZOM-42; Robert's dynamic difficulty deck; TierManager.cs

Assigned when a player's 10th game ends (wins and losses both count, not 10 levels cleared). Average CPM over those 10 games > 90 moves them to tier 1; everyone else, including exactly 90, stays on tier 0.
Build (TierManager.ApplyInitialBucketing) + Blake's 30 Sep reply. The deck and ZOM-199 say 90 or more after the first 10 levels; the build wins.

Tier -2 is an exception: you promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player and promote if the win rate is 80% or higher (early exit: 8 wins in a row is enough without playing all 10). The record resets to 0 games after every promotion or demotion.

Lose 4 in a row and you are demoted one tier, at any time. You are also demoted when your win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower (early exit, e.g. LLLWLL). A 60-70% win rate neither promotes nor demotes. The record resets to 0 games after every demotion.

Yes, it drops: on top of the tier going down one, the level the player was on loads one further tier version down on the next attempt, until they win (the retry offset resets on a win and is not saved between sessions).
A blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages every monster on the board, including ones spawned after. Enrage adds walk speed and damage per monster; the HP boost is off (0).

The baseline is in the ZM Difficulty folder: <https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1V1ENBGOnCDQpm3578LUam9DJmTSDhMfo8Js4KMHPO6g/edit|ZM difficulty baseline register>. It has two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force. Robert can edit, you and Brian can comment, and Arthur can view.

*24 tickets made the list:* 16 Live, 4 Editor only, 1 Replaced, 3 Not shipped.
• *Not shipped:* ZOM-202, ZOM-280, ZOM-293
• *Editor only:* ZOM-173, ZOM-200, ZOM-277, ZOM-315
• *Replaced:* ZOM-254 was replaced by ZOM-282. ZOM-282's closing note says it replaces the Blunder 2.0 boost: enrage is speed and damage only now, HP is off.

*Starting tier:* a new player gets it when their 10th game ends, with wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. Average CPM over those 10 games has to be above 90 for tier 1. Exactly 90 stays on tier 0, along with everyone else. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck both say 90 or more after the first 10 levels, so I went by the build.

Ticket comments: ZOM-199 got a note on what the build actually does. ZOM-254 got a note naming ZOM-282. The editor only and not shipped tickets each got a note saying the change isn't in iOS 0.3.49 / Android 0.3.133.

What's off the list: everything you named (30, 49, 50, 161, 162, 163, 201, 250, 258, 262, 275). Also ZOM-312, because Blake marked it "not tiers" in his review on its PR, and ZOM-203 and ZOM-276, which are duplicates. ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378 are on the list because of Blake's "tiers:" closing notes.

Enrage numbers are copied from the Live tab of the enrage sheet as it stands. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl show as not copied yet.

content.text:
I built the register, put it in the ZM Difficulty folder, shared it, commented on the tickets and replied to Leonard in his DM thread.

**What's in the register** ([ZM difficulty baseline register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1V1ENBGOnCDQpm3578LUam9DJmTSDhMfo8Js4KMHPO6g/edit)):
- It has two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force, as the session agenda asks.
- The Tickets tab has the columns from Leonard's card, plus the three Robert asked for in your group chat: assignee, done date in Pacific time, and Linear priority.
- **24 tickets made the list:** 16 Live, 4 Editor only, 1 Replaced, 3 Not shipped.
  - Not shipped: ZOM-202, 280, 293.
  - Editor only: ZOM-173, 200, 277, 315.
  - Replaced: ZOM-254, by ZOM-282. ZOM-282's closing note says it replaces ZOM-254's enrage boost, so enrage is now speed and damage only.
- **Starting tier:** Blake's email and the code agree that it's set when a new player's 10th game ends (wins and losses both count). The player needs an average above 90 clicks per minute for tier 1, so exactly 90 stays on tier 0. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck both say "90 or more after 10 levels"; the card says to go by the build, so I did.
- The enrage numbers are copied from the Live tab of your monster enrage sheet as it stands. Mailman, Mayor2 and PartyGirl are marked "not copied yet."

**Leonard changed the rules three times after writing the card. I followed his latest word each time:**
- He took 11 tickets off the list: 30, 49, 50, 161, 162, 163, 201, 250, 258, 262, 275. None of them got comments.
- He added "attack power" in the title as a match.
- Brian was going to get edit access, then Leonard said comment is enough. Arthur only needs view.

**Sharing:** Robert can edit, Leonard and Brian can comment, Arthur can view.

**Ticket comments (9 in total):**
- ZOM-199 got a note on what the build actually does.
- ZOM-254 got a note naming ZOM-282 as its replacement.
- The 4 Editor only and 3 Not shipped tickets each got a note that the change isn't in iOS 0.3.49 or Android 0.3.133.

No other tickets were changed.

**Calls I made you should know about:**
- I left ZOM-312 off: although the title matches, Blake wrote "not tiers" on its pull request. ZOM-203 and ZOM-276 are off because they're duplicates.
- I added ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378 even though their titles don't match, because Blake's closing notes mark them as tier work.
- Some tickets are marked Done in Linear but are listed as Editor only, because Blake's notes or emails say the change was only in the level editor or debug menu. Players never get those.
- I marked ZOM-199 Live: new players do get a starting tier, just under slightly different rules than the ticket says.
- ZOM-263 isn't linked to any pull request. I marked it Live because attack power is shown to players, but Robert may want to confirm that in the session.
